subject: Telemetry redaction governance follow-up: trace IDs & retention carve-outs
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@carecorp.com>, dlp-security@carecorp.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Telemetry/data handling discussion - next steps

Alex / CareCorp team — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the logging & redaction asks you raised.

Key points from call:
- Scope: Request/response logs captured by Redwood's proxy layer (ingest + post-call logs), including select headers.
- Primary concerns: PII in payloads, trace IDs in headers (used for debugging), and retention windows for telemetry.
- Compliance drivers: CareCorp's internal DLP requirements + upcoming audit; preference for minimized retention and proof of redaction.

What Redwood can provide (high level):
- Configurable header scrubbing: we can strip or pseudonymize trace IDs at ingest. Pseudonymization options: deterministic hash, salted hash (customer-managed salt), or full redact.
- Field-level redaction: request/response can be redacted via regex rules, and we can maintain a short-lived KV for troubleshooting.
- Retention windows: default telemetry retention is 90 days; we can propose a 30-day retention for redacted telemetry under a higher SLA tier.
- Evidence for audit: we will provide audit logs showing when redaction rules applied and a digest (hash) proof for removed values.

Open decisions / asks for CareCorp:
1) Decide whether trace IDs need to be retained (hashed) for incident investigation or fully redacted. If retaining hashed IDs, do you require customer-managed keying/salt?
2) Target retention window for telemetry used in debugging (30 / 60 / 90 days?)
3) Any specific headers or payload fields that must never be logged (please send a short list or examples).

Proposed next steps (suggested timeline):
- CareCorp: confirm answers to Q1–Q3 by EOD Friday (2027-05-21).
- Redwood engineering (Marissa): provide a short technical note with examples of hashed vs redacted trace IDs and performance impact by 2027-05-18.
- Run a 1-week POC where we ship sanitized example logs and show audit evidence (target week of 2027-05-31).

I attached an initial redaction requirements draft and a short SOW for the POC. If that timeline looks good I can book a 30-minute check-in next week to walk the engineering team through the options.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0148

Date: 2027-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Telemetry/data handling discussion - next steps

Thanks for the clear summary, Sergio — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) Trace IDs: our preference is to retain a usable identifier for investigation, but we cannot store the raw trace ID in a reversible form tied to user PII. A deterministic hash would be acceptable if we can supply the salt (customer-managed) and have evidence that the raw value was redacted.

2) Retention: for telemetry used for debugging we prefer 30 days, but we can consider 60 days for major incidents if we have a documented escalation path.

3) Headers: Please ensure Authorization-like headers are never persisted. Also, we will send a short list of endpoints and JSON fields (PII examples) — expect that from us by Wednesday 2027-05-19.

Two asks from our compliance team (cc'd):
- DLP wants the audit record format you mentioned; ideally a signed digest that proves redaction occurred and which rule matched.
- They also request a sample of the evidence you can provide (redacted sample log + audit line) before the POC.

If you can get Marissa's technical note by Tuesday and the sample evidence shortly after, we can lock the POC for the week of 2027-05-31.

Alex Morgan
Senior Security Program Manager | CareCorp Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-17T10:44:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Technical note: hash vs redact options + sample evidence

Sergio / Ben — drafting the short tech note now; posting the answers here so you can share with CareCorp.

Technical options we can demonstrate in the POC:
- Full redact: strip the header/value at ingest and emit an audit record that includes a rule id, timestamp, request id, and redaction status. No traceable identifier remains in logs.
- Deterministic salted hash: compute H = HMAC_SHA256(salt, trace_id) and store only H in logs. We can keep the salt customer-managed via KMS integration (supporting AWS KMS and GCP KMS). With customer-managed salt we cannot derive the raw trace id from Redwood side; we can still match records during support with cooperation from CareCorp.
- Ephemeral troubleshooting store: for customers who need short-term reversibility, we can keep an encrypted kv-store for up to N days (configurable). Keys rotated monthly; access logged.

Performance impact: hashing at ingest adds ~1–2ms per request at our current throughput (measured on our staging fleet). Ephemeral kv lookups add latency if requested during hot paths; we propose async lookup or a debug-only path.

Audit evidence sample (we will attach a redacted sample log in the POC):
- Log line: {timestamp} {service} {request_id} trace_id=<HMAC_SHA256(salt,****)> redaction=hashed rule=header_traceid_v1
- Audit line: {timestamp} user=redwood-system action=redact_match rule=header_traceid_v1 evidence_hash=<sha256 of removed_value>

Questions for CareCorp to confirm:
A) Do you require the evidence_hash to be revocable by Redwood (i.e., Redwood can provide the raw value to legal ops) or must that capability be restricted to CareCorp only?
B) For ephemeral store: maximum retention you want for reversible troubleshooting (suggested default: 7 days).

I'll attach the technical note and a redacted sample by EOD 2027-05-18.

-Marissa

Subject: Agreed next steps + POC kickoff prep (telemetry redaction)

Alex — thanks for confirming. Quick summary of what we agreed and immediate asks so we can start the POC prep: 

Agreed: 
- Use deterministic salted hash for trace IDs during the POC, with CareCorp-managed salt via AWS KMS. Redwood will not retain the raw trace id in any persisted logs.
- Telemetry retention for the POC = 30 days. Ephemeral troubleshooting store enabled for 7 days (encrypted, access logged).
- Redwood will provide signed audit lines (digest evidence) for every redaction event in POC.

Action items: 
- CareCorp: share the list of sensitive headers/fields and confirm DLP contact for legal/ops (Alex already cc'd dlp-security).
- CareCorp: confirm whether Redwood should implement the HMAC salt in your KMS or if you will supply the salt material to Redwood (preference: KMS grants to Redwood service account).
- Redwood: Marissa to attach the technical note and sample evidence by EOD 2027-05-18 (attached).
- Redwood sales/ops (Ben): I'll attach the draft SOW and cost estimate; please review and confirm any procurement requirements.

If you can confirm the KMS approach and share the header list, I'll schedule the POC kickoff (30 min) for 2027-05-31 and loop in our infra lead.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.
